items.text: Quasi-affine schemes: equivalent conditions
$X$ coherent, $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, $j\colon X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Equivalent:
(a) $X$ quasi-affine; (b) $X$ has a morphism to an affine scheme which is a monomorphism and a homeomorphism onto its image (then $j$ is an open immersion).
(c) $\mathcal O_X$ is ample: the $X_f$, $f\in A$, form a basis; (c$'$) the affine $X_f$ form a basis; (d) every quasi-coherent sheaf (or ideal) of finite type is generated by its sections.
(e) there is an invertible $\mathcal L$ with $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal L^{-1}$ ample.
Quasi-affine morphisms
$f\colon X\to Y$ quasi-affine: $Y=\bigcup Y_i$ affine with $X_i$ quasi-affine; i.e. $\mathcal O_X$ ample relative to $Y$.
f\ \text{coherent (even separated) and}\ \ f^*f_*\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\ \text{surjective for every quasi-coherent }\mathcal F
Stable under base change and composition (no quasi-compactness needed: local on $Z$); quasi-compact immersions and affine morphisms are quasi-affine.
An immersion is quasi-affine iff quasi-compact. $g\circ f$ quasi-affine, $g$ quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ $f$ quasi-affine.
Zariski's main theorem (as stated)
$f$ of finite type, separated, with finite fibres (quasi-finite without separated) $\Rightarrow$ quasi-affine; and if $Y$ is coherent,
f=f'\circ i,\quad f'\colon X'\to Y\ \text{finite},\quad i\colon X\hookrightarrow X'\ \text{quasi-compact open immersion}
Proved by global methods (finiteness theorems for proper morphisms); out of scope here.
Radicial morphisms
$f\colon X\to Y$ equivalent: (a) $f$ is universally injective (injective after any base change);
(b) for each $y$ at most one $x$ above it, and $\kappa(x)/\kappa(y)$ radicial (purely inseparable);
\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k\ \text{universally injective}\iff\forall k'\ \exists\ \text{at most one }k\text{-hom }K\to k'\iff K/k\ \text{radicial}
(c) $X(K)\to Y(K)$ injective for every field $K$;
(d) the diagonal $\Delta_f\colon X\to X\times_YX$ is surjective.
\text{surjective}\iff\text{every geometric point of }S\ \text{lifts, after field extension, to a geometric point of }T
Stable under base change and composition; monomorphisms are radicial; $g\circ f$ radicial $\Rightarrow$ $f$ radicial.
Universal homeomorphisms
$f$ integral, radicial, surjective $\Rightarrow$ universal homeomorphism (universally bijective and closed); conversely universal homeomorphisms are integral (affine), radicial, surjective.
Examples: $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $k'$ the perfect closure; the normalization of a cuspidal curve ($x^2+y^3=0$).
A homeomorphism that is not universal: $\tilde Y\to Y$ the normalization of a node, $X=\tilde Y\setminus\{y_1\}$; $X\to Y$ is bijective and a homeomorphism.
\tilde Y\times_Y\tilde Y=\tilde Y\ (\text{diagonal})\ \sqcup\{z_1\}\sqcup\{z_2\},\qquad X\times_YX=X\sqcup\{z_i\}\ \text{(an isolated point)}
Open morphisms
$f$ universally open: open and stays open after any base change; stable under composition and base change. (The map above is open but not universally open.)
$f$ open $\Rightarrow$ for all $x\in X$, $y=f(x)$:
\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Y,y}\ \text{surjective}\qquad(f\ \text{is generalizing})
Every generalization $y'$ of $y=f(x)$ lifts to a generalization $x'$ of $x$.
Proof: $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}=\bigcap U$ (affine opens $U\ni x$), $f(U)\supset\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Y,y}$; images commute with such intersections.
Lemma: images and inverse limits
$X\to Y$, $X_i\to X$ affine forming an inverse system, $Z=\varprojlim X_i$, $g_i\colon X_i\to X$, $g\colon Z\to X$:
f\bigl(g(Z)\bigr)=\bigcap_i f\bigl(g_i(X_i)\bigr)
Proof: $Z_y=\varprojlim X_{i,y}$ (base change commutes with inverse limits).
